Assets

USTB is live on X Layer. The rest is research.

USTB publishes to X Layer mainnet and testnet every day, and both of its policies currently read CONFIRMED. OUSG, FOBXX and USDY are research, each with the exact retrieval problem that stands between it and a daily publication. Statuses here are facts, not aspirations: an asset is called live only once a signed report for it is on chain.

In research

A brand name is not an ingestion contract. Each of these has a measured retrieval surface and one problem left to close; none of them is published until that problem is closed.

Research

OUSG

Ondo Short-Term U.S. Government Treasuries

The fastest credible second asset: a bounded issuer page with real business-day movement and no archive dependency. Its evidence is issuer-published HTML rather than a documented JSON API, so extraction anchors have to be selected and pinned before a control can quote a byte span from them.

Research

FOBXX

Franklin OnChain U.S. Government Money Fund

The daily issuer endpoint is refused at the production host — Cloudflare answers 403 — so the daily path is closed. A monthly path through the fund's SEC N-MFP3 filings is scoped and carries a committed fixture: evidence filed with a regulator, at the cadence a money-market fund files it.

Research

USDY

Ondo U.S. Dollar Yield

The issuer source is one 260 MB unbounded archive. A daily window cannot be pointed at an unbounded retrieval, so USDY stays in research until a bounded route is proven and measured.

What “live” means here

A live asset has a signed report on both X Layer registries, published by a run that read the issuer at a named moment and stored every fetch as a digest-addressed capture. Reports expire at the end of the UTC day and re-publish at the daily window, so a reader is never handed yesterday's answer dressed as today's. Freshness is the product, not a caveat.

Adding an asset is retrieval work, not contract work: the registry is already multi-asset and the control language is already asset-agnostic. The constraint is a single operator running one daily window, and it is published here rather than implied.
